target.title: fix(voice-call): normalize mapped proxy addresses
target.body:
Closes #86525
Supersedes #86527 because the contributor fork predates the current `main` history and cannot be refreshed through GitHub's verified branch-edit path without replaying unrelated repository history.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where voice webhooks arriving through an IPv4 socket could be represented by Node as an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address, preventing a configured trusted IPv4 proxy from being recognized.

## Why This Change Was Made

Webhook signature verification and the media-stream path now share one narrow proxy-address normalizer. Only IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals are converted; ordinary IPv4 and IPv6 addresses retain their existing representation and trust checks.

## User Impact

Operators using trusted IPv4 reverse proxies can validate carrier webhook URLs correctly even when Node reports the peer as `::ffff:a.b.c.d`.

## Evidence

- Focused local voice-call suites: 70/70 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox focused suite: 67/67 tests passed.
- Real IPv4 TCP socket probe produced `::ffff:127.0.0.1`; the production Twilio verifier accepted the reconstructed public proxy URL and returned a verified request key.
- Twilio and Plivo webhook proxy/signature contracts were checked against their current official documentation.
- Fresh Codex autoreview: clean, 0.99 confidence.
- Original contributor credit from #86527 is preserved in the commit.

Known proof gaps: none for the bounded address-normalization path.
